thread:
Maya: Quick heads-up — since the deploy at ~07:10 UTC I'm seeing a pattern where prefetcher worker traces have the root span but almost none of the child spans (KV get, deserialization). Jaeger shows the request trace id but child spans missing. Anyone seen this before? Linking dashboards + an example trace: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/xyz/prefetcher-overview and https://jaeger.redwood.com/trace/abcd1234

Jason: Which prefetcher service + sampler config? Probabilistic sampling could drop children if they start outside parent context.

Maya: Service: prefetcher-worker-prod (k8s). Using otel-java 1.23 auto-instrumentation + custom code that wraps async tasks with CompletableFutures. Sampler: ParentBasedTraceState + probability 0.01. In canary region we see normal child spans, only prod seems affected.

Anita: Any errors in exporter logs? OTLP exporter overload or auth errors can silently drop spans. Can you paste worker logs around those trace IDs?

Maya: No obvious OTLP errors. Sample from worker log: 
```
2026-03-12T07:11:05Z INFO processing job id=123 trace_id=abcd1234
2026-03-12T07:11:05Z DEBUG AsyncExecutor submit taskId=xyz
2026-03-12T07:11:05Z DEBUG KVClient get key=user:42 (no span started)
```

Ron: Two quick suspects: 1) context not propagated across Executor/CompletableFuture, 2) sampling decision differs between services/hosts. The auto-instrumentation may depend on context storage mechanism — are you running on a patched JVM or using our opentelemetry-javaagent?

Maya: We're using the javaagent on prod nodes (same as canary). I wonder if there's pressure on the worker thread pool leading to tasks scheduled on common ForkJoinPool which might lose context. We also have a custom wrapper that calls executor.submit(() -> { .. }) from a Netty thread.

Jason: If tasks are scheduled on threads where context isn't attached, child spans won't be linked. Two quick checks: 1) search logs for "otel.context" or errors from otel-context-storage, 2) enable DEBUG for io.opentelemetry.context to see context attach/detach.

observability-bot: Dashboard quicklinks: Prefetcher traces panel: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/xyz/prefetcher-overview?var-service=prefetcher-worker-prod. Traces filter: service=prefetcher-worker-prod AND has_child_spans=false. CPU heatmap: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/xyz/prefetcher-cpu

Anita: Also check sampler config in the Collector. We had one case where sampler was set at the collector to drop all non-root spans when span count > N to protect collector memory. Not default, but config drift possible between regions. Can someone grep collector config in prod?

Maya: Good call — looks like collector in prod has com.redwood.sampler.max_payload_spans=5000 set by an old emergency patch. Canary doesn't. Could that cause child span drops?

Ron: Yes, if the collector enforces a tail-sampling or quota that truncates spans per-trace, you could see only the root exported. Check collector logs for messages about "span export limit" or "truncating spans".

Jason: Another quick test: in a dev pod, add an explicit child span around KVClient.get to verify it shows up when you force context propagation:
```java
Span span = tracer.spanBuilder("kv-get").startSpan();
try (Scope s = span.makeCurrent()) {
  kvClient.get(key);
} finally {
  span.end();
}
```
If that appears in Jaeger, the issue is propagation/sampler, not instrumentation hook.

Maya: Ran that locally, explicit child span shows up. So likely propagation or collector sampling in prod. I'm going to roll a quick patch to avoid submit() -> wrap with Context.current().wrap(Runnable) before submitting.

Anita: If you patch, also add a metric to count started spans per job so we can alert on sudden drop (alert: prefetcher.span_count drop > 50% over 5m). I'll put a quick PR for the metric + an ops runbook note.

ci-bot: CI pipeline started for PR #4723 (maya/prefetcher/propagate-context). Status: running tests. https://ci.redwood.com/builds/4723

Ron: After patch, let's watch the grafana panel and set a temporary low-friction alert to pager if child-span ratio < 0.6 for 10m, so we catch recurrence.

Maya: Thanks all — patching now and will post back with collector logs & PR link. If anyone on-call wants to pair to grep collector config, ping me. :thumbsup:

Jason: Thanks Maya. If collector is the culprit, we should add region config checks to our infra linting.

Anita: I'll open an infra ticket to sync collector configs across regions and add a unit test for sampler params in our infra repo.

Maya: Update: PR green, deployed to staging, child spans returned. Will deploy to prod tomorrow morning under a short maintenance window. Will also follow up with collector config audit.

Ron: Nice — appreciate the quick turnaround. :rocket:
